mechanism: The University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment (headline UMCSENT) is a survey measure of household economic optimism. Rising sentiment precedes stronger spending and risk-on equity conditions; falling sentiment precedes retrenchment. The strategy holds SPY when sentiment is favorable.
key_finding: Best search-phase rule uses diff_1m at L12 with OOS Sharpe 1.25 versus buy-and-hold 0.95.
caveats: Winner is search-selected on a single monthly sample and needs holdout validation.
Lead grid is floored to L1 (#255 publication-lag discipline); the searched grid is the contiguous shifted grid [1..13].
Level/change thresholds are rolling-percentile based; regime pivots can drift across decades.
Lead estimates rest on a limited number of cycles in the sample.
narrative_summary: U. Michigan headline consumer sentiment is tested as a procyclical sentiment overlay for SPY. NEW pair; compare with umcsent_xlv (same series vs XLV) and umcsent_spy (expected-business-conditions diffusion vs SPY).

data_provenance.source: FRED (University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers)
